transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I'm just really struggling with how my skin looks, especially these horrible scars and acne on my face. It feels so ugly and noticeable to me, even though my family keeps telling me my skin looks completely normal. I just can't stop worrying about it.
How much time each day do you spend thinking about your skin, and do you find yourself doing repeated things like checking mirrors, picking at your skin, or avoiding people because of it?
I easily spend several hours every single day obsessing over these flaws on my face. I constantly check the mirror to inspect my skin, and I often end up picking at it to try and smooth it out.
Aside from worrying about your skin, have you been feeling depressed most days or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?
I'm not really sure about that, to be honest. I haven't really thought about whether I'm depressed because my mind is just so constantly consumed by how bad my skin looks.
Besides concerns about your skin, do you also have other unwanted repetitive thoughts or rituals, like fears of contamination, checking, counting, or needing things to feel just right?

No, I don't experience anything like that. I don't have fears about contamination, and I don't feel any need to count things or arrange items to feel just right. My anxiety is really just focused on my skin and how my face looks.
Do you think your skin really looks abnormal to other people, or is part of you aware that the concern may be stronger than what others actually see?

I am absolutely certain that my skin looks genuinely abnormal and that everyone can see these terrible flaws. Even though people tell me it's not a big deal, I know they are just trying to be polite and spare my feelings. The scars and acne are just too obvious to me for my concerns to be exaggerated.
When you feel distressed about your skin, do you do repetitive things like mirror checking, comparing your appearance to others, seeking reassurance, or trying to hide the area?

Yes, I do all of those things constantly. I spend hours checking my skin in the mirror, comparing it to everyone else's clear skin, and repeatedly asking my family for reassurance that it doesn't look awful. I also have to spend a massive amount of time using heavy makeup and hats to camouflage the flaws before I can even think about leaving the house.
How much has this affected your daily life—for example, do you avoid school, work, social situations, or leaving the house because of your skin?

I haven't really thought about whether I completely avoid those situations, but I do spend hours trying to hide my skin before I can even step outside. It makes going to work or seeing friends incredibly stressful, and I'm always late because of it.
Aside from believing your skin looks abnormal, do you have any other strong beliefs that others are talking about you, staring at you, or trying to harm or deceive you because of it?

I don't think anyone is trying to harm or deceive me, and I don't have any paranoid thoughts like that. I do sometimes worry that people might notice my skin defects or stare at my face because it looks so bad, but I know they aren't plotting against me.
Have you ever sought dermatology or cosmetic treatments for your skin, and if so, did you still feel distressed or dissatisfied even after doctors said it looked normal or treatment helped?

Yes, I have been to multiple dermatologists and even had several expensive cosmetic procedures to fix these scars, but nothing seems to work. Even though the doctors insisted my skin looked completely normal and that the treatments were successful, I still felt deeply distressed and unsatisfied. The flaws still look incredibly obvious and ugly to me, no matter what they say.
